Lo these many years ago when I was in community college and taking a basic municipal law course the instructor said, of laws in general, that "they must not only be fair, but they must be seen to be fair". The same rule, I believe, should apply to election campaigns.

On the face of it I can see why Elections Canada might say that

.....there’s nothing wrong with the Conservative party employing the services of controversial Australian campaign fixer Lynton Crosby.

He is, after all, not directly inducing voters to vote one way or another in the upcoming election - then again,

The Canada Elections Act specifies that it is illegal for anyone who is not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident to “in any way induce electors” to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate.

And there it is, that inconvenient "in any way...." bit.

If we were looking at a crime, lets say bank robbery, and I was being paid to advise someone on the best way to break into a particular bank, grab the loot, and make a clean get away to a non-extradition country where they could live in the lap of luxury for the rest of their lives the law would most certainly consider that I was part of the act. And try me accordingly.

We see the same sort of thing in the [CPC candidate] Alain Rayes campaign where his father is also the assistant returning officer for the electoral district. It may be, and probably is (as Rayes says) the case that the man is

..... simply continuing the work he's been doing since before I even thought of entering federal politics.

But that's not the point, and both the CPC campaign and Rayes should know that.

In the first case I linked there is the perception that Stephen Harper and the CPC are flouting Canadian Election law, I know that perception is there because I've seen it all over different social media venues. I realize that Stephen Harper is not happy with seeing his name in the 3rd place position but his decision in this, as technically legal as it may be, does nothing but bolster the "win at all costs" judgment many have already leveled at him.

In the second case the assistant returning officer may, or may not, have any real pull in how ballots are organized and counted on election night, but there is already the perception that he may have just enough pull to swing things his sons way if needed. Again, we are confronted with the "win at all costs" judgment many have already leveled at the Harper campaign.
